main_turf.bias_notes: Clockwise (right-handed). A notoriously tight, fast-turning SE Queensland oval with a short 300m home straight. The track features a long, sweeping turn starting from the 1000m mark all the way into the short straight. This geometry generates a massive natural bias toward early speed ('E') and pocket pressers ('P') holding the fence. Deep closers ('Swoopers') frequently run out of stretch length.
main_turf.post_bias: INSIDE BARRIER BIAS: Inside barriers (stalls 1–4) are an immense advantage. Horses drawn wide (8+) are forced to either burn significant early energy to cross over or get caught wide on the continuous sweeping turn, which is a steep penalty.

handicapping_angles.the_bundamba_speed_bias: Heavily upgrade pure early speed ('E' types) and rail-skimming tactical stalkers ('P'). Aggressively downgrade deep closers ('Swoopers'), as the 300m straight rarely gives them enough runway to reel in leaders.
handicapping_angles.specialist_track_form: Because the shape is so unique and tight, 'Horses for Courses' is a massive angle. Upgrade horses with proven winning form specifically at Ipswich (+3.0 pts), as large-striding gallopers often fail to handle continuous cornering.
handicapping_angles.se_qld_metro_alternate_and_ipswich_cup: Ipswich serves as a primary Metro alternate for Brisbane yards (Tony Gollan, Matt Hoysted, Chris Waller). During the June Ipswich Cup ($250k+ Listed) & Eye Liner Stakes feature meeting, race quality elevates to Metro/Listed grade.
